summary: Isomer's PhotosUI is the SwiftUI photo picker: `.photosPicker(isPresented:selection:…)` asks the host's own picker (a file input on the web, the system photo picker on Android) for photos and videos, which come back as `PhotosPickerItem`s whose bytes `loadTransferable(type:)` reads as `Data` or a `URL`, with `PHPickerFilter` saying which kinds. It is compiled over each platform's SwiftUI. On Apple platforms an app uses Apple's PhotosUI (its SwiftUI picker is the PhotosUI–SwiftUI cross-import overlay).
deviations: A picked item's identifier is the picked file's path (its name, through `itemIdentifier`), not a photo library asset's: there is no photo library.
`selectionBehavior` and `preferredItemEncoding` are taken and left to the host's picker.

groups.title: The PhotosPicker view and picker styling
groups.why: `PhotosPicker` (the button that presents the picker), the inline and compact picker styles, and the picker's accessory, capability, metadata and search options. The modifier form covers what apps use most; the view is the next step.

groups.title: More filters
groups.why: The photo library's finer kinds (bursts, panoramas, slow motion, screen recordings, …) and `all(of:)`/`not(_:)`: the hosts' pickers filter by MIME type, so these narrow nothing yet.

groups.title: Equatable and loading by callback
groups.why: The value types' synthesized equality and hashing as Apple declares them, and `loadTransferable(type:completionHandler:)` (the async form is there).

groups.title: UIKit and AppKit pickers and views
groups.why: `PHPickerViewController`, its configuration, results and delegate, `PHLivePhotoView`, the content-editing controller and the shared-album view controllers are UIKit and AppKit classes; Isomer's platforms have neither. The SwiftUI picker is the cross-platform form.

groups.title: Photo library views and sheets
groups.why: The shared-album sheets and the reference image viewer work on Apple's photo library, which Isomer's platforms do not have.

additions: Isomer's PhotosUI declares nothing Apple's lacks; anything listed here is a regression.
